applicability.execution_path: IDENTICAL, which is why this is proven and not reused: every observation was taken in the same CTP invocation, against the same client-server server process, in the same session sequence as the assertions it supports. TWO CHANNELS, recorded under channel `other` because the schema carries one channel per row. (1) SHOW HEAP OOS after the committed INSERT and again after the restart (show_heap_oos_after_insert.out, show_heap_oos_after_recovery.out beside the reference) certifies the INSERT-side demotion -- one OOS file, four chunk records for four rows -- and the presence of the chains after recovery. (2) The server's own recovery log for this database ($CUBRID/log/server/<db>_*.err, copied into the bundle as case-evidence/server_log/ and excerpted in the reference) certifies that the RECOVERY PATH RAN AND REPLAYED WORK: exactly one new 'Log recovery: REDO Phase is started' line after the restart, with 'Log pages to redo: 2, Log records to redo: 83', and 'Log pages to undo: 0, transactions to undo: 0'. Channel (2) is what the independent review's F1 asked for: without it the values could have survived because the pages were flushed before the kill -9, and the specification says proof of an insert path never certifies a recovery path. Neither channel certifies a vacuum or reclaim path, which is why the post-recovery chunk count is asserted as a range.
